body: Confirmed cross-browser reproduction on Chrome 145 and Firefox 148.0.2 (macOS), March 2026. Clean PoC with confirmed code execution: ```js const d = document.createElement('div'); d.appendChild(document.createComment('-->` sequence in the comment data is not escaped during serialization. `d.innerHTML` produces: ``` ``` Re-assigning to `d2.innerHTML` breaks the comment boundary and creates a live `` element. The `onerror` handler executes. Confirmed with `alert(1)` popping in both browsers. This differs slightly from the PoC in the issue - no `+=` on `document.body.innerHTML` needed. A simple detached div round-trip is sufficient to trigger code execution when the result is inserted into a live document node. Attack surface: any application that copies DOM via `innerHTML` round-trip where user-controlled data can influence comment node creation - Vue `v-if`/`v-for` anchors, React/Next.js Suspense boundaries (`$`/`/$` comment markers), Angular structural directives. DOMPurify 3.1.6 strips the `onerror` attribute but leaves the `` element, so sanitizer pipelines that don't re-sanitize after deserialization remain at risk.
